lines: Keep your hands off the map table unless you know where they are going.
Give the map table room. Mapping works better without elbows in it.
Step carefully near the map table. I would rather greet you than patch you up.
There you are. I was just near the map table, trying to keep the day sensible.
Morning. Or afternoon. The work makes the hours blur if I let it.
Good to see you walking in calmly. That usually means nothing is on fire yet.
If you need me, speak up. If you need gossip, speak quieter.
You caught me before the next little disaster. That is rare timing.
Hello. Try not to bring the whole village into this unless it is important.
I have a moment. Not a long one, but a real one.
Mind the table. The ink is fresh and unforgiving.
Hello. If you moved the compass, please confess gently.
You caught me between one road and the next mistake.
Step lightly. I am trying to keep the world flat for a moment.
Good timing. The map was getting too confident.
Welcome. Try not to lean on the wet corner.
I have ink on my fingers and a little time for questions.
If you came with directions, I already doubt them politely.
There you are. I was just arguing with a coastline.
Stand where you are. I need the light more than the company.
Hello. The road can wait if you cannot.
Keep clear of the quills unless you want to become a landmark.
I am listening, though half my mind is still north of here.
Come closer, but do not breathe on the ink.
The table is crowded, but I can make room for a short talk.
